rows.citation: Yang, C. (2026). A Judge Agent Closes the Reliability Gap in AI-Generated Scientific Simulation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2603.25780 [cs.SE].
rows.model_type: general AI-generated scientific simulation code across 12 domains (PDEs, stiff ODEs, inverse problems, CT); no neuron models found in full-text scan
rows.controlled_mutations: no - uses 50 hand-built adversarial problem inputs (ambiguous or subtly ill-posed specs), not recorded single-fault operators applied to models.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - each task is one specified computational problem; no battery of input stimuli applied to the same model.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - checks well-posedness, convergence, error bounds and physical invariants; no spike or voltage-trace features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - Judge applies fixed pre- and post-execution gates; no selection of a compact discriminating test set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: yes - checks designed on 12 development problems, then evaluated on 72 blinded tasks submitted by external scientists.
rows.ai_transformations: yes - LLM agents plan and generate simulation code; the Judge targets silent failures in that AI-generated code.
rows.software: Physics_World_Model - https://github.com/integritynoble/Physics_World_Model (paper states MIT; GitHub API license field NOASSERTION)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Certifies numerical validity of newly generated code; NeuroSem compares an edited neuron model against its reference using mutant-calibrated, selected current-clamp batteries and eFEL features.
rows.verification_method: DataCite API for 10.48550/arXiv.2603.25780 (Crossref: not found; arXiv export API returned 503); arXiv HTML full text v1 (https://arxiv.org/html/2603.25780) keyword-scanned; GitHub REST via gh for repo.
rows.found_via: Semantic Scholar API search 'AI coding agent neuron simulation'; arXiv abs page fetched via WebFetch

rows.citation: Stockton, D. B., Prinz, A. A., & Santamaria, F. (2019). Provenance and Reproducibility in the Automation of a Standard Computational Neuroscience Pipeline. Proceedings of the 2nd International Workshop on Practical Reproducible Evaluation of Computer Systems (P-RECS), 7-12.
rows.model_type: computational neuroscience simulation workflows managed by NeuroManager; specific neuron models not verified (abstract only)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - abstract describes workflow automation and provenance capture; no fault injection or mutants reported.
rows.multiple_stimuli: unclear - automates simulation scheduling across servers, clusters and clouds; stimulus design not described in abstract, full text blocked.
rows.electrophysiology_features: unclear - pipeline spans experiment, data, modeling and analysis; feature extraction not detailed in the abstract.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - abstract mentions no selection or optimisation of test or stimulation protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - reviews the authors' tooling work; no held-out evaluation described in abstract.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-generated or AI-edited models mentioned.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Concerns provenance and job automation for running simulations; NeuroSem could borrow run-provenance practice but adds behavioural-change detection via mutants, protocol selection and held-out tests.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (metadata); Semantic Scholar API (abstract); GitHub REST via gh (repo search and metadata); ACM DL PDF returned a Cloudflare challenge, so full text not read.

rows.citation: Wilsdorf, P., Wolpers, A., Hilton, J., et al. (2023). Automatic Reuse, Adaption, and Execution of Simulation Experiments via Provenance Patterns. ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation, 33, 1-27.
rows.model_type: general simulation models: agent-based migration-route model and SBML ODE Wnt/beta-catenin signaling models
rows.controlled_mutations: no - model versions come from real study development (successive model extensions), not systematic single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - automatically re-runs prior experiments (sensitivity analysis, cross-validation under a transient stimulus); not a designed perturbation battery.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - outputs are sensitivity indices and protein trajectories; electrophysiology mentioned only as related work.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - provenance rules choose which existing experiments to reuse and adapt; no optimisation for discriminating power or cost.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstrated through two case studies; no held-out models or mutation families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - rule-based provenance-graph transformations; no AI-edited models.
rows.software: RASE (Java, Neo4j) - https://git.informatik.uni-rostock.de/mosi/exp-generation (URL cited in arXiv version; responded HTTP 200, contents not inspected)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Automates re-running earlier experiments after model change (framed as regression testing); NeuroSem additionally calibrates tolerances and uses mutants to choose which stimuli detect changes in neuron models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (metadata and abstract); Semantic Scholar API (arXiv id 2109.06776); arXiv PDF full text keyword-scanned; OpenAlex reports publisher version closed access.

rows.citation: Midingoyi, C. A., Pradal, C., Athanasiadis, I. N., et al. (2020). Reuse of process-based models: automatic transformation into many programming languages and simulation platforms. in silico Plants, 2, diaa007.
rows.model_type: process-based crop model components (CyML unit models) transformed into Fortran, C#, C++, Java, Python, R and crop modelling platforms
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no fault injection; translation correctness is checked by running the model's own unit tests in each target.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - specifications allow several unit tests with different parameter sets; baseline parameter sweeps explicitly unsupported.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - crop process models; outputs compared to expected values within a stated precision.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - unit tests are author-written; no selection of a compact discriminating test set.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - demonstrated with a simple unit model; no held-out models or mutation families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - deterministic rule-based source-to-source transformation, not AI-assisted.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Checks translations against fixed per-model unit tests; NeuroSem asks whether such limited tests miss behaviour changes and selects neuron stimulation batteries using mutants and held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (metadata and abstract); OpenAlex OA locations; full-text PDF from WUR repository (https://edepot.wur.nl/540614) keyword-scanned (OUP pages blocked); GitHub REST via gh.

rows.citation: Lei, C. L., Whittaker, D., Windley, M., et al. (2024). A range of voltage-clamp protocol designs for rapid capture of hERG kinetics. Wellcome Open Research, 9, 673. [version 2, 2025]
rows.model_type: hERG (Kv11.1) ion-channel gating ODE models (Beattie and Wang Markov structures); voltage clamp
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no fault-injected models; designs use two candidate model structures and fitted parameter ranges.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - suite of short step/ramp voltage-clamp protocols (staircase, square-wave, sensitivity-based, action-potential-like) for one channel.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - works with simulated ionic currents and parameter sensitivities; voltage clamp, no current-clamp spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - automated designs optimise protocol parameters to maximise parameter sensitivity or differences between two candidate models.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - design paper; experimental data and assessment are in a partner publication, not evaluated here.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-edited or AI-generated models.
rows.software: protocol-design-hERG - https://github.com/CardiacModelling/protocol-design-hERG (BSD-3-Clause per GitHub API and paper); archive https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.13343099 (DataCite lists CC-BY-4.0)
